question: A marketing analyst asks Claude for a sales summary for executives who want only key trends and decisions, not methodology, but the first draft includes several paragraphs on data cleaning. How should the analyst refine the prompt for this audience?
options: A) Ask Claude to keep the structure but shorten every paragraph by a similar amount
B) Ask Claude to move the data cleaning paragraphs to a footnote at the end of the summary
C) Ask Claude to expand the cleaning explanation so executives can verify it themselves
D) Ask Claude to lead with the trends and decisions and drop the data cleaning explanation
correct_answers: D) Ask Claude to lead with the trends and decisions and drop the data cleaning explanation
explanations: Incorrect. Uniformly shortening every paragraph keeps the irrelevant methodology section in the summary instead of removing it.
Incorrect. Moving the methodology to a footnote still includes content the executives do not want instead of leading with what they need first.
Incorrect. Expanding the methodology section moves the summary further from what a time-constrained executive audience wants.
Correct. Executives want trends and decisions, so restructuring the summary to foreground that content and dropping methodology detail matches the stated audience need.
